claims: FISA Section 702 allows warrantless targeted intelligence gathering on non-Americans located abroad.
FISA Section 702 was authorized under the 2008 FISA Amendments Act.
FISA Section 702 allows the government to compel U.S. companies (e.g., Google, AT&T) to provide access to communications of targeted foreigners outside the U.S.
FISA Section 702 inevitably captures data on U.S. citizens while targeting foreigners.
Government agencies including the FBI have used FISA Section 702 to search for American information without a warrant.
The FBI has faced criticism for "widespread violations" of rules including searching for data on protesters, journalists, and political donors.
FISA Section 702 is set to expire in April 2026.
FISA Section 702's 2026 reauthorization is stalled over privacy concerns specifically regarding "backdoor searches" of American data by federal agencies.
FISA Section 702 is used for counterterrorism and cybersecurity.
The U.S. says the wiretap program thwarted an attack on the 2024 Taylor Swift Concert.
A court's ruling requires the agencies to re-engineer the filter tools to comply with rules for queries for Americans' information.
Congress will soon vote on the reauthorization of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.
Trump wants the FISA law extended
